Doom.title: Doom Clock
Doom.atMidnight: The Doom Clock is already at Midnight.
Doom.atClear: The Doom Clock is already Clear.
Doom.newCycle: A new Doom Cycle begins (cycle {cycle}). The clock is Clear.
Doom.newCycleConfirm: Reset the Doom Clock to Clear and start a new Doom Cycle? Once per Doom Cycle abilities recharge.
Doom.eventsHint: Players don't see these on screen, and each one is whispered to the GM when the clock reaches its mark. Foundry stores all world data where a player using the browser console could read it, so don't rely on this to keep spoilers from a determined player.

Status.tryRemove: Try to remove (uses an Interact Action)
Status.turnWounds: {status}: {n} wound(s) at the start of the turn

StatusHint.afraid: Lose 1 Core Skill Point from every skill (minimum 1). Steady your nerve with a Fear Check.
StatusHint.terrified: Lose 2 Core Skill Points from every skill (minimum 1). Two successful Fear Checks to be Stable.
StatusHint.bleed: X wounds at the start of each Combat Turn. Interact: Smarts CR 2 to stop.
StatusHint.burning: X wounds at the start of each Combat Turn. Interact: Grit or Wit CR 1, or water.
StatusHint.poisoned: X wounds at the start of each Combat Turn. Interact: Grit CR 3 (lower with medical help).
StatusHint.blinded: Fail checks that need sight; -1 Skill Die on attacks. Ends after your next turn.
StatusHint.stunned: No actions on your next turn. Ends after that turn.
StatusHint.prone: Your actions have Minor Disadvantage; attacks on you have Minor Advantage. Slow, half move. Move Action to stand.
StatusHint.grappled: No Move or Attack. Interact: opposed Grit to break free.
StatusHint.maimed: Speed Slow. Interact: Smarts CR 2 to remove.
StatusHint.crippled: Speed Slow, permanently, until extensive medical care or healing magic.
StatusHint.cursed: Can't heal wounds until the source is killed or destroyed.
StatusHint.taunted: Must attack or pursue the source on your next turn.
StatusHint.vengeance: The enemy with Vengeance has Minor Advantage attacking you.
StatusHint.infected: Turning into the monster that infected you. X is the stage (0-4); click the virus icon to set the infection.
StatusHint.stealth: Move halved; enemies have Major Disadvantage to spot you; a Strike from Stealth has Major Advantage.
StatusHint.hidden: Out of sight. If an enemy comes within 5 ft, Wit CR 1 to stay still.
StatusHint.deathsDoor: Unconscious at 0 Health. Roll the Luck Pool each turn: one success keeps you alive.
StatusHint.unconscious: Out cold until the threat has passed or more healing is given.

Uses.nextCycle: recharges with a new Doom Cycle

Combat.deathsDoorTurn: {name} is at Death's Door: roll the Luck Pool.
Combat.noActions: {name} can't take any actions this turn.
Combat.grappled: {name} is Grappled: no Move or Attack Actions; use an Interact Action to break free (opposed Grit).
Combat.escapeHint: Uses an Interact Action. Every enemy in the Brawl may make a free attack; a Grapple or Prone stops you getting away.
Combat.escapeText: {name} tries to Escape the Brawl. Free attacks from: {enemies}. If any of them Grapples or knocks {name} Prone, the Escape fails.
Combat.grappleHint: Opposed Grit Check against your target. The winner makes the loser Grappled.

Death.door: {name} is unconscious at Death's Door. On each of their turns they roll the Luck Pool: one success keeps them alive. An ally can stabilise them with healing or a CR 2 Smarts Check.
Death.stabilised: {name} is stabilised at 1 Health and unconscious.

Nightmare.weakenedHint: Lifeline quarter lost: -1 Core Skill Point in a chosen skill until healed.
Nightmare.limpingHint: Lifeline half lost: Speed is Slow until healed.
Nightmare.traumaHint: Three quarters lost: -1 Talent Point in a chosen skill, or lose an ability, until healed.
Nightmare.weakenedPrompt: Weakened: choose a Core Skill to lose 1 Core Skill Point until this quarter is healed.
Nightmare.traumaPrompt: Trauma: choose a Core Skill to lose 1 Talent Point, or choose to lose an ability instead.
Nightmare.traumaAbility: lose the use of an ability (choose with the Director)
Nightmare.traumaAbilityPrompt: Trauma: choose the ability you lose until this quarter of the Lifeline is healed.

Reaction.title: {name} reacts
Reaction.hint: When hit, the Director rolls one Skill Die. The enemy reacts only on the faces lit by its Deathcon level. Luck never reacts unless this enemy has its own Luck entry.

Weapon.takeAim: Take Aim (Interact): Minor Advantage on the next Strike
Weapon.stunMode: Stun: deal 1 Blunt instead; the target is Stunned

Item.rulesHint: Automation rules the system applies for this item. Rules marked as notes are reminders for the table.

Tree.title: Archetype Tree: {name}
Tree.removeConfirm: Remove this ability and refund its Ability Point?
Tree.noPoints: No Ability Points left. Each Character Level gives one.
Tree.notConnected: That ability isn't connected to one you have in the tier below.
Tree.spendPoints: Spend {n} Core Skill Points: all on one skill, or split between two.
Tree.hybridHint: Needs 5+ permanent Core Skill Points in the Archetype's skill (a Talent Point counts as 2; the Survivor needs two skills). At most three Archetypes. Each one costs a unique Fatal Flaw.
Tree.hybridNeeds: Needs {n} of these at 5+ permanent points: {skills}
Tree.fatalFlawPrompt: Choose the Fatal Flaw this costs:
Tree.maxArchetypes: A character can have at most three Archetypes.
Tree.chooseTalent: Choose the Core Skill that gains {n} Talent Point(s).
Tree.chooseTier1: Choose your Tier 1 ability. It takes your first Ability Point.
Tree.notYourArchetype: {name} isn't one of this character's Archetypes. Hybridise first (Archetype Tree).
Tree.alreadyOwned: The character already has this ability.

Sheet.crHint: Your Challenge Rating: how many successes it takes to hit you.
Sheet.lifelineHint: Click a box to mark wounds up to it.

modeOfPlay.name: Mode of Play
modeOfPlay.hint: Survivor Mode: at 16 wounds a character falls unconscious at Death's Door. Nightmare Mode: each quarter of the Lifeline lost brings a penalty, and 16 wounds is instant death (p.15).

storyLevel.name: Story Character Level
storyLevel.hint: The Character Level new characters start at (1-15, p.30).

doomAtMidnight.name: Doom Clock at Midnight
doomAtMidnight.hint: What happens to further ticks once the clock reaches Midnight.
doomAtMidnight.hold: Hold at Midnight until the Director starts a new cycle

fearCheckStrangeDoom.name: Failed Fear Checks tick Doom per Strange symbol
fearCheckStrangeDoom.hint: A failed Fear Check adds 1 minute (p.19). With this on, its Strange symbols also tick the clock like any failed check (p.11).

autoReactions.name: Roll Enemy Reactions automatically
autoReactions.hint: Roll a Reaction for every hit on an enemy, whispered to the GM (p.26).

autoOverwhelm.name: Detect Overwhelm
autoOverwhelm.hint: Lower a Large-or-smaller enemy's CR by 1 when three or more characters are within 5 ft of it (p.23).

playersApplyDamage.name: Players can apply damage
playersApplyDamage.hint: Let players press Apply Damage on their own Strikes, and let their abilities' damage reach other characters. When off, only the GM applies damage to characters a player doesn't own.

hideEnemyDamage.name: Whisper enemy damage to the GM
hideEnemyDamage.hint: Keep enemy damage numbers and Health hidden from players (p.121).

enemyCrits.name: Enemies can crit
enemyCrits.hint: Let enemies' Strikes against characters be Critical Hits and Full Houses.

enforceTree.name: Enforce Archetype Tree rules
enforceTree.hint: Archetype abilities need an Ability Point, a connected ability in the tier below, and the right Archetype, however they are added.

infectionMethod.name: Infection tracking
infectionMethod.hint: Doom Clock: infections advance one stage each Doom Quarter (p.192). Lifeline: the Director sets the stage.

enforceRange.name: Enforce weapon Range
enforceRange.hint: Strikes can only target tokens within the weapon's Range (p.22, p.129).

Malfunction.title: {item}: Malfunction
Malfunction.grit: Jammed: the attack resolves, but your next Move Action must go to unjamming it before it can be used again.
Malfunction.wit: Lowered Guard: the attack resolves, but the next attack against you has Major Advantage.
Malfunction.smarts: Break: the Strike hits, but the weapon deals half damage until repaired.
Malfunction.heart: Stumble: the attack misses whatever you rolled, and you fall Prone.
Malfunction.strange: Backfire: you take half the weapon's damage.
